scope: Dimension 3b: what a section DOES, classified from content as well as heading. Section LOCATION lives in section_registry.json and is a source-address registry, not a taxonomy. One section may perform several functions; a heading can be absent, generic or misleading; the same function can recur under different labels in different families.

functions.DEFINITIONS: Defines terms, formulas or quantities used elsewhere.
functions.SERVICE_LEVELS: States the committed service level, objective or target and how it is measured.
functions.FEES_AND_PAYMENT: States prices, invoicing or payment terms.
functions.EXCLUSIONS: Lists circumstances carved out of a metric, commitment or remedy.
functions.SERVICE_CREDITS_AND_REMEDIES: States the remedy for a service-level failure, its amount, form, limits and exclusivity.
functions.CLAIM_PROCEDURE: States how and when a remedy must be requested and what forfeits it.
functions.INTERPRETATION_AND_SCOPE: States how terms are read, who the parties are for this document and which incorporated documents control undefined terms.
functions.VERSION_AND_APPLICABILITY: States which version applies to whom and from when.
functions.OTHER_UNKNOWN: No function can be assigned from the available evidence.

rules: A function label requires at least one content quote anchored in the frozen packets; a heading alone is not evidence.
Section location (heading, numbering, path, anchors) is recorded separately and never changes when a function label changes.
Function labels stay PROVISIONAL; they confer no legal meaning on the provisions inside the section.

lineage.reason: initial taxonomy seeded from the owner's examples plus INTERPRETATION_AND_SCOPE and VERSION_AND_APPLICABILITY observed in the frozen packets
